PART I - D
GENERAL SPECIFICATIONS

THIS IS A REQUIREMENTS CONTRACT. ALL TASKS AND WORK ORDERS WILL BE
ASSIGNED ON AN-AS NEEDED BASIS.

Article 1 DESCRIPTION OF WORK
The work to be performed under this Contract (“Agreement” or “Contract”) includes furnishing all labor, materials, travel time, equipment and all other work incidental thereto necessary or required to provide the complete testing, maintenance and repair of Automated Logic WebCTRL and Carrier I-Vu Building Automation systems and equipment at various NYC Parks facilities Citywide.

Article 2 CONTRACTOR’S QUALIFICATIONS/EQUIPMENT LIST
I. Certification and Experience
The Contractor shall have been in continuous business for a minimum of three (3) years prior to the bid opening date, actively and commercially providing the full scope of services required under this contract, including those related to project size and complexity. In the case of a joint venture, at least one member of the joint venture must meet this three (3) year minimum requirement. Prior to award, the Contractor must submit the names and contact information of at least three
(3) client organizations that can verify the Contractor’s successful experience in providing services comparable in scope and scale to those required under this contract.
II. Equipment List
The Contractor shall possess and make available all tools, equipment and instruments necessary to make repairs and/or upgrades on all required parts and equipment covered under this contract. CERTIFICATION OR MEMBERSHIP: If these specifications require certification by, or membership in, a non-governmental entity or organization, the contractor shall possess either that certification or membership, or equivalent qualifications or characteristics as determined acceptable by the Agency. This provision does not waive any legally required Federal, State, or local certifications or licenses, nor does it alter any requirement for manufacturer-specific certification of materials or equipment where such certification is specified.

Article 3 TERM OF CONTRACT
The term of this contract shall run for five (5) years from the Order to Work (“OTW”) date set forth in the Notice to Proceed with the Work (also known as the Order to Work Letter).

Article 4 SCOPE OF WORK
A. General
The Contractor shall cooperate with the Project Manager on the premises: to prevent

unauthorized persons from entering said premises; to ensure that the Contractor and its workers comply with all applicable Agency rules and regulations; to avoid unnecessary dust, or accumulated debris; to prevent the Contractor’s personnel and/or work performed thereby from interfering with regular Agency operations at such buildings and facilities; and, to take necessary precautions to prevent the loss or damage of property at such buildings. Use of electricians and plumbers shall require approval from the Project Manager prior to the commencement of any electrical or plumbing work being performed. The Contractor shall supply his employees working at the facility with uniform displaying the company name. In addition, the Contractor’s employees shall at all times prominently display on their uniforms their respective Contractor issued, employee picture identification Cards, which shall each bear the Contractor’s name, a color photograph of the respective employee, the typewritten name of the respective employee, and the typewritten trade classification the respective employee. The Contractor shall notify the Project Manager of any planned visit to the site/s at least twenty-four (24) hours prior to its serviceperson’s expected arrival time. With the exception of emergency requests, all work is to be performed during regular working hours between 8:00 am and 5:00 pm, Monday through Friday, with the exception of paid holidays, unless otherwise agreed by the Project Manager.
B. Maintenance
Maintenance at all facilities shall include but not be limited to the following:

1. AUTOMATION NETWORK
a. Review for proper communications at operator workstation, server, and all global controllers.
i. Check all network and communications performance
b. Check alarm logs and correct errors.
c. Upgrade software to the latest version (either WebCTRL or I-Vu as applicable).
i. All licensing costs shall be included in the “Regular Maintenance” fee and shall not be charged separately.
d. Perform complete system device upload to archive and ensure that archive data is up to date.
e. Perform full system backup; one copy shall be retained on site and one copy shall be retained by the vendor.
f. Provide summary report of system performance to the Project Manager. Report any deficiencies and recommend appropriate corrective measures.

2. CONTROLLERS: for all controllers listed under Appendix A.
a. Review individual control loops.
b. Check all LED indicators for:
i. Power levels;
ii. Transmit and Receive activity on all trunks;
iii. Error Codes; and

iv. Sequencing regarding self-test displays or Error Code indications.
c. Check to ensure all batteries (clock, data protection, data detection) are performing as required, replace as necessary.
d. Check wiring for signs of corrosion, fraying and rapid discoloration.
e. Check and ensure secureness of all trunk / field point connections.
f. Check the system for active alarms and report to appropriate personnel.
g. Confirm communication status/reliability with system.
h. Confirm on-line status of field points and reliability of data points.
i. Review system diagnostics for confirmation of reliable on-line performance.
j. Verify database archive is up to date, utilizing system configuration tool to update archive.
k. Verify on-line status and calibration of Analog Input / Binary Input device(s) and record in Facility Management System log.
l. Perform backup of controller.
m. Clean interior and exterior surfaces (including removal of dust and debris from heat sink surfaces), as well as the area surrounding equipment.
n. Complete maintenance checklist.
o. Report any deficiencies to the Project Manager and recommend appropriate corrective measures.

3. VAV (Variable Air Volume ) Boxes
a. Check with the Project Manager for any known operational deficiencies.
b. Verify on-line status.
c. Remotely verify VAV box sequence of operations. Verify box program.
d. Check operation of box with BAS (Building Automation System) (if applicable).
e. Remotely check damper motor operation.
f. Complete required maintenance checklist.
g. Report any deficiencies to the Project Manager and recommend appropriate corrective measures.

4. VERIFY ALL CRITICAL SYSTEM SENSORS (AIRSIDE/WATERSIDE) SUCH
AS, BUT NOT LIMITED TO ITEMS LISTED:
a. Calibrate or replace all failed temperature, humidity, and CO2 sensors at no additional cost. All other required sensor replacements shall be considered repair and reimbursable if the material cost is less than $150 and the replacement requires less than 4 hours to complete:
i. Outside/Indoor air temperature sensors;
ii. Supply temperature sensors;
iii. iii. Return temperature sensors;
iv. CO2 sensors;
v. Pressure switches;
vi. Humidity sensors

Sensor Failure, for the purposes of this item, is defined as any of the following:
• Sensors that exhibit extreme highs or lows as seen on the BMS (Building

Management System) front end;
• Outdoor air sensor measurements that differ significantly from local weather conditions; or
• Manual IAQ (Indoor Air Quality) measurements taken by Parks personnel that differ more than 3 degrees F, 5% RH, or 50 PPM CO2 from the sensor reading on the BMS.
5. AIRFLOW STATIONS AND WATERFLOW METERS:
a. Verify functionality
b. Calibrate or replace as needed

6. TEMPERATURE SENSORS:
a. Verify functionality.
b. Calibrate or replace as needed.

7. SPACE THERMOSTATS:
a. Verify functionality of space thermostats, at least 10% during each maintenance visit, prioritizing those located in rooms from which the Project Manager receives complaints.
b. Calibrate or replace as needed

8. ACTUATORS FOR DAMPERS AND VALVES:
a. Test actuators and witness responses airflow/water flow changes
b. Provide detailed findings
c. Replace/repair as needed

9. MISC. PARTS (Fiber optic Hubs, Uninterruptible Power Supply, Printer, other components):
a. Clean interior & exterior surfaces.
b. Review for proper operation.
c. Report any deficiencies to the Project Manager and recommend appropriate corrective measures.
d. Report other BAS deficiencies

NYC Parks reserves the right to request the Contractor to perform maintenance at any of the sites listed herein at any time by providing the Contractor a Work Order for such Work. It is anticipated that maintenance shall be performed at the following intervals to the approval of the Project Manager:
Gracie Mansion:
The Contractor shall perform six (6) evenly spaced scheduled maintenance visits per year. Flushing Meadows Corona Park Pool/Rink:
The Contractor shall perform four to six scheduled maintenance visits per year during the term of this Contracr. Carmine Carro:

The Contractor shall perform four (4) scheduled maintenance visits per year. The Contractor shall visit the site.. Each visit shall be approximately three months apart.
C. Scheduled and Unscheduled Service/Repairs The Contractor shall provide non-scheduled service as may be required whenever requested by the Project Manager. The Contractor shall commence service at the job site within two (2) business days of when requested. Failure to respond within the appropriate time frame will result in liquidated damages as defined in Article 8.
WORK ORDERS
The Agency shall submit to the Contractor a Work Order Request Form that shall be recognized as a valid authorization to commence work by signature of the applicable Project Manager or Authorized Site Representative. Once the work described on the Work Order Request has been completed and the equipment has been restored to service, the Contractor shall obtain signature of the applicable Project Manager or Authorized Site Representative validating the work is complete. No payment will be made if the Contractor does not provide a fully completed and executed Work Order Request Form(s) with the corresponding invoice. The Contractor shall be required to verify the arrival time and departure time of its workers at each site by completing the appropriate area of the Contractor Sign-in Sheet that shall be presented to the Contractor at each work site. (See, e .g., Attachment A “Work Order Request Form”, Attachment B “Sample Contractor Sign-in Sheet”). Upon departure for the work site, the Contractor shall have his/her time on site validated by signature of the applicable Project Manager or Authorized Site Representative. No payment will be made if the Contractor does not provide fully completed and validated Contractor Sign-in Sheet(s) with the corresponding invoice. The Contractor shall start work within two (2) business days after receipt of a work order. For emergencies, the Contractor shall be required to respond within four (4) hours from the placement of the call or Work Order. The Contractor is expected to work each consecutive business day until the work is completed. The number of workers employed on any work order shall be the minimum required to perform the work adequately and safely and will be subject to approval by the applicable Project Manager or Authorized Site Representative before work is started. The time spent on each work order will be verified by the Agency. In case of multiple work orders, the Contractor will be advised by the Project Manager as to the priority of each work order. The Contractor shall submit a written cost proposal for each project/work requested to the applicable Project Manager or Authorized Site Representative for their review. This cost proposal shall be itemized and show each Item, Quantity, and Unit Price as per the contract Bid Page. Once the Agency Project Manager or Authorized Site Representative accepts the proposal, they will submit a Work Order Form to the ACCO’s (Parks Contracts Division) Office for final approval and funds encumbrance. Once approved, the ACCO’s Office will send the approved Work Order Form to the Contractor.

Once the Contractor receives the approved signed Work Order Form, it can perform the work outlined in the Work Order and proposal. Any changes or additions to an issued approved Work Order Form, must be done via a new Work Order Form. The Contractor shall NOT honor any verbal Work Orders or changes to an existing Work Order Form from the Agency Project Manager or Authorized Site Representative or any other Parks staff. This is to ensure that the necessary funds for each issued Work Order are encumbered, and payments to the Contractor can be issued once the work is completed. Failure to adhere to this policy may result in non-payment to the Contractor.

WORK TICKET
The Contractor's designee shall leave a Work Ticket with the Project Manager or Authorized Site Representative at the job site. This Work Ticket will give a brief description of the work performed, date, time, hour(s) at the job site, parts used and the name of the service person(s) who performed such work. This Work Ticket shall be signed by the Agency on site, upon completion and approval of the work. A copy of the completed Work Ticket(s) must be submitted with the Contractor's monthly invoice. The Contractor's failure to submit Work Ticket(s) with its invoice may result in a delay in payment.
ESTIMATES
At times, the Contractor shall be required to supply Parks with a free estimate prior to the issuance of a work order. The Contractor shall not proceed with the work until the estimate is approved by the Project Manager, and a Work Order has been issued.
WORK LOCATIONS
The Agency may instruct the vendor to provide and perform all services in any borough of the City and in any NYC Parks facilities. The locations for service are stated in Article 4 “Scope of Work”, under Section A- General Info.

Article 5 MEASUREMENT AND PAYMENT
The Work to be performed under this contract includes furnishing all labor materials, travel time, equipment and all other work incidental thereto necessary or required for to provide the complete testing, maintenance and repair of Automated Logic WebCTRL and Carrier I-Vu Building Automation systems and equipment at various NYC Parks facilities Citywide.
ITEMS # 1-3: SCHEDULED MAINTENANCE SERVICE
Bid Items 1-3 cover the following Work:
A. Onsite training support, operator assistance, and general consultation services.
B. Standard and emergency (24 hour) telephone support.
C. The vendor must provide, and complete, maintenance check lists that mirror the required maintenance tasks as delineated in this Contract. The unit price bid shall include all costs including profit, overhead, administration, equipment, transportation (to and from sites), tolls, parking, employee labor time and any other incidental cost not specifically mentioned but necessary for the performance of work under this Contract

in accordance with the scope of work.
The Contractor shall receive payment only upon completion of each maintenance service and submission of a comprehensive report and all completed checklists. in accordance with Article 16 “Invoices and Reports”.
ITEM # 4, 7, 8, 9 and 10: LABOR RATES MONDAYS- FRIDAYS All equipment that is required to be used under these items shall be included under the unit bid prices. This includes, but is not limited to, all tools and supplies necessary for services as outlined in the Contract.
ITEM # 5: SYSTEM SPECIALIST LABOR RATES AFTER HOURS AND
SATURDAYS
All equipment that is required to be used under these items shall be included under the unit bid prices. This includes, but is not limited to, all tools and supplies necessary for services as outlined in the Contract.
ITEM # 6: SYSTEM SPECIALIST LABOR RATES SUNDAYS AND HOLIDAYS
All equipment that is required to be used under these items shall be included under the unit bid prices. This includes, but is not limited to, all tools and supplies necessary for services as outlined in the Contract. Item #11 Materials/Parts and Equipment Rental

Under these items, the Contractor shall furnish materials. The Contractor shall replace or repair worn parts or obsolete components with new parts, unless directed otherwise by the Project Manager. It is understood that this applies only to the systems and mechanical equipment covered in this Agreement. It is further understood that after the systems have been put into proper operating condition, by the Contractor, he/she will not be responsible to make replacements or repairs necessitated by reason of negligence or misuse of the equipment by others or by reason of any other cause beyond the Contractor’s control except ordinary wear and tear. The material shall match the original in all respects. All material to be furnished under these items shall be subject to the prior written approval of the Project Manager” The lump sum price indicated on the bid page, plus profit and overhead, is an estimated amount for materials and may vary from the amount actually expended for the cost of materials for renewals or replacement during the term of the Contract. Payments will be made ONLY upon presenting clear and legible copies of the Contractor’s suppliers’ bills or invoices detailing the materials, its purpose, location where installed, including the date it was installed. In addition, the Project Manager shall have the right to pay less than the costs submitted by the Contractor for materials when it is determined that the Contractor should have been able to purchase such materials at a lower cost than actually paid by the Contractor. Item #12 & 13 Profit and Overhead In addition to the lump sum price indicated in the bid book, the Contractor shall bid a percentage for overhead and profit over the cost of materials for repairs. Such percentage shall

not exceed 10%. Overhead and profit shall include, but not limited to, all taxes and standard (non-express) freight.

Article 6 SUBCONTRACTING
No subcontracting shall be permitted without prior approval by the Agency Chief Contracting Officer (ACCO). Subcontractor Approval Process:
The City uses the PASSPort system to review and approve Subcontractors, Subcontractor updates, payment validation, and M/WBE utilization tracking. The Contractor must submit all Subcontractor approval requests via PASSPort. The Agency will review and approve Subcontractor requests directly in PASSPort. The Contractor shall not cause a Subcontractor to perform any Contract Work until such Subcontractor has received final Agency approval in PASSPort. If a Subcontractor starts Work without final PASSPort approval, the Agency will disapprove payment for the Work performed by such Subcontractor. When Subcontracting is approved:
All required notices, Work Orders, directives and requests for services will be issued to the Contractor. The Subcontractor shall be bound by the same terms and conditions of the Contract as the Contractor. Contractor and their Subcontractors shall also abide by all Contract terms and conditions. The Contractor shall submit any changes/updates to previously approved Subcontractors via PASSPort. In no event shall the prices charged to the Agency for subcontracting Work exceed the Contractor’s corresponding price(s) bid for such Work. The Contractor shall record payments made to Subcontractors via PASSPort. All Subcontractor invoices must be submitted to the Contractor with all of the applicable the items specified in Article 14 herein entitled, “Invoices and Reports.” The Contractor shall submit with its invoices clear and legible copies of all suppliers’ invoices including Subcontractors' invoices for Work performed. The Agency reserves the right to require the Contractor to terminate the services of a Subcontractor at any time.

Article 7 INSPECTION
The Agency shall conduct an inspection of all work to ensure compliance with the Contract’s specifications. The Project Manager has final discretion for approving all work for payment. No partial payments will be made for incomplete or unsatisfactory work. After the inspection is completed and the Contractor is notified in writing by the Agency, the Contractor has two (2) business days from the date of notification to complete any incomplete or unsatisfactory work.

The Agency reserves the right to hold the invoice if there is any incomplete or unsatisfactory work outstanding. The City will not pay any interest on the invoices that are held due to incomplete or unsatisfactory performance of the Contractor.

Article 8 LIQUIDATED DAMAGES IN CASE OF DELAY
1. If the Contractor fails to:
a) Complete preventive maintenance on the upon the agreed upon scheduled, unless the Project Manager agrees to an extension in writing;
b) Commence equipment repair work specified within the Contractor’s cost proposal approved by the Project Manager and the corresponding work order issued by the Project Manager for specific requested work order by the timeframe set forth therein; or
c) Diligently perform and satisfactorily complete Work Orders, in accordance with the provisions of this Agreement, particularly those set forth in Article 4 thereof, by, before or on the completion date, set forth in such Work Order by the Project Manager, which completion date, the Project Manager shall have reasonably established, based on the information in the cost proposal that the Contractor submitted to the Agency pursuant to its request for the specified work; then the Contractor shall be assessed liquidated damages in the amount of $100 per day per incident.
2. However, the Project Manager may extend any date for work to commence or be completed, at their discretion, should the Project Manager reasonably determine that, through no fault of the Contractor, such extension is necessary to address circumstances beyond the control of the Contractor. For a full list of liquidated damages that apply to this Agreement please see the Schedule A.

Article 9 OPTIONAL SITE VISIT
On request, prospective bidders will have the opportunity to examine the equipment at the sites. A request must be made by contacting Justin Hicks, Contracts Analyst, 212-830-7983 and justin.hicks@parks.nyc.gov. An escorted visit will be arranged at that time. Under no circumstances will a bidder be permitted to visit any site unaccompanied by official Agency personnel. In no event will a failure to inspect the site constitute grounds for disqualification of a bidder.

Article 10 AWARD OF CONTRACT
In the sole discretion of the Agency, the award of the Contract will go to the lowest responsive, responsible, and qualified bidder to perform the work as outlined in these specifications. All bidders will be evaluated to determine if they have the resources and manpower to perform the work of this Contract. The Contractor must possess the qualifications and equipment outlined in Article 2. The Contractor will be found non-responsible if the Agency finds that he/she does not have sufficient resources or manpower. The Agency reserves the right to award this Contract to the next lowest responsive and responsible bidder if the original Contractor is found to be non-responsive and /or non-

9. Work Ticket (Completed by Contractor) - When applicable;
10. Receipts from suppliers for parts and materials - When applicable; and,
11. Certified Prevailing Wage Payment Sheet - When applicable. Payments for materials/supplies will be based on originals of invoices of the cost of materials, plus, when allowed in the bid page, a percentage bid for overhead and profit combined. All payments shall be subject to audit by the Agency and to post-audit by the Comptroller's Office. In order to facilitate post-audit by the New York City Comptroller's Office, the Contractor agrees to maintain adequate fiscal records of its expenditure under this Agreement for a period of six (6) years from final completion unless notified otherwise by the Agency.

Article 15 PRECAUTIONS TO BE TAKEN/PUBLIC UTILITIES The Contractor must take precautions against any injury to people and damage to property. All work shall be done to least inconvenience the public and property owners. The Contractor shall cooperate with City Agencies and utility companies to ensure that service is not disrupted. The Contractor is responsible for giving prior notification to all City Agencies and utility companies whose services may be impacted by the work.

Article 16 DAMAGE CLAIMS
The Contractor shall be responsible for, and shall repair or replace any part of the Agency property damaged during the performance of the work. In addition, the Contractor shall repair or replace any damages to sidewalks, cars, and any other property caused by the Contractor’s operation. The Contractor shall notify the Agency of any damages by the end of the business day on which such damage occurred. All damage shall be repaired within two (2) weeks. The Agency reserves the right to withhold payment on all outstanding invoices until all of the above requirements are met.

Article 17 ASSIGNMENT
The Contractor shall not assign or transfer, by operation of law or otherwise, this Agreement or any rights or obligations hereunder without the prior written consent of the Agency Chief Contracting Officer.

Article 18 FAILURE TO PERFORM
The Agency reserves the right, during the term of this Contract, to have this work performed by other Contractors, if this Contractor is unable to perform any specific work order within the time period provided. The Agency may deduct from any money owed to the Contractor pursuant to this Contract, the additional cost, if any, of replacement work. Failure to complete a work order within the time specified by the Project Manager may result in liquidated damages and/or the cancellation of this Contract by the City of New York.

Article 19 PRE-AWARD MEETING
The Agency hereby reserves the right to hold a pre-award meeting with the apparent lowest bidder to verify that all requirements of the Contract are fully understood.

Article 20 PREVAILING WAGES & CERTIFICATION OF WAGE AMOUNTS
(WHEN APPLICABLE AS NOTED ON THE SCHEDULE A)
The wages, which the Contractor shall pay for a legal day's work and supplements to be provided to workers as defined in Section 220 and/or Section 230 of the Labor Law, employed upon the whole or part of the installation, construction repair and/or maintenance work contemplated by this Contract, shall not be less than the prevailing rate of wages and any supplements required to be paid to the various classes of employees on such work, ascertained and determined by the Comptroller. No later than the first day upon which work on this Contract is to commence, the Contractor shall post in a prominent and accessible place on the site of work a legible statement of the wages to be paid to the employees for the electrical repair and maintenance work contemplated. An apprentice in a craft or trade may be permitted to work at a wage lower than that established for the journeyman in such craft or trade only if all of the following conditions are met:
(1) such apprentice has been individually registered in an apprenticeship program which is duly registered with the New York State Industrial Commissioner in conformity with Article 23 of the Labor Law;
(2) such apprentice's registration occurred prior to his/her employment as an apprentice on such craft or trade service work; and
(3) written proof of such individual registration is submitted to the Agency prior to such apprentice's employment as an apprentice. The proof submitted shall include evidence of the appropriate ratios and apprentice's wage rates. In no event shall the ratio of apprentice to journeyman employed on such service work be greater than the lesser of the following ratios:
(a) the ratio permitted in the apprenticeship program approved by the industrial commissioner, or (b) the ratio prevailing in the locality where the service work will be performed. The obligation of the Contractor to pay prevailing supplements may be discharged by furnishing any equivalent combinations of fringe benefits or by making equivalent or differential payments in cash under rules and regulations established by the fiscal officer.

CERTIFICATION OF WAGE AMOUNTS
As a prerequisite to any payment by the City, the Contractor shall file a statement in writing and in form satisfactory to the Comptroller, certifying to the amounts then due for daily or weekly wages on account of labor performed upon the work hereunder, setting forth therein the names of the persons whose wages are unpaid and the amount due to or on behalf of each respectively, which statement so to be filed shall be certified by the oath of the Contractor, that he has read such statement subscribed by him and knows the contents thereof, and that the same is true of
